chunks: And the confirmation of this is what Ṣafwān narrated from Murāzim regarding a man who gives something from his wealth during his illness.
He said: 'If he clearly transfers it (during his lifetime), then it is valid. However, if he bequeaths it (for after his death), then it is only from one-third of his wealth.'

key_terms.أَبَانَ: To make clear, to manifest, to clearly transfer possession
key_terms.أَوْصَى: To bequeath, to make a will
key_terms.الثُّلُثِ: The third (one-third), referring to the portion of estate available for bequests

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between a gift and a bequest when given during illness in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* establishes the critical legal distinction between *hibah* (gift) and *wasiyyah* (bequest) in the context of illness (*marad al-wadi'*). It clarifies that a gift is fully valid and not subject to the one-third limit if the donor clearly manifests their intent to transfer ownership while alive, whereas bequests remain capped at one-third to protect heirs' rights. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the donor's explicit declaration (*ibanah*) in determining the nature of the transaction.
